selector.name: PLAYER_INTERACTION_ANIMATION_INDEX
selector.contract: The contact resolver clears the byte on ordinary contact and increments it for left/right push responses, wrapping after 0x27. The selector masks the low two bits, so values 0x00, 0x04, ..., 0x24 select table entries 0 through 9.

table.name: PLAYER_INTERACTION_ANIMATION_TABLE
table.targets: The ten longwords point to PLAYER_ANIM_INTERACTION_VARIANT_00 through PLAYER_ANIM_INTERACTION_VARIANT_09, each with a contiguous ten-byte prelude ending in the shared terrain-alignment continuation.

static_evidence: The 0x001A9B38 instruction sequence reads 0x00FFF16A, masks the low two bits through an 0xFFFC byte offset, loads a longword from 0x001218D8, clears PLAYER_ANIMATION_TIMER, and writes TERRAIN_HORIZONTAL_RESPONSE=2.
The 0x001A99F0 instruction sequence increments 0x00FFF16A on directional push branches and wraps values above 0x27 to zero.
The exact 0x001218D8-0x001218FF table and all ten selected stream roots are already bounded by lossless animation decoding.
conclusion: The former DAT_00FFF16A byte is now a canonical RAM symbol, and the interaction-animation table has a confirmed exact extent and mask-based selector contract.
